newsitem.title: UK: Metals wobble during LME pre-market then stabilise.
newsitem.headline: Metals wobble during LME pre-market then stabilise.

text.p: Base metal prices initially lurched lower during Tuesday LME pre-market trading, extending the previous day's declines, before stabilising in line with copper.
Traders said copper veered worringly under $1,920 at one stage, with a technical objective of $1,910 in the market's sights. But a 7,825-tonne stock decline, although expected, promoted a mini-rally.

The current pressure reflects last week's rebuff near $2,000 and consequent speculative selling. Also, the cash/threes spread has reverted to a contango after a brief backwardation, while Wednesday's October option declarations are less of a concern.
But although the market is now well below the $2,000 strike, there will still be some caution ahead of the option expiries.
Prices touched a low of $1,917 a tonne before settling recently at $1,924, still down $8.
Elsewhere a 950-tonne fall in aluminium stocks bucked the recent trend of increases and caused a temporary halt in the market's decline, which saw fresh 2-1/4 year lows notched up.
But there is little consumer offtake at present and prices are expected to fall towards $1,360 and $1,350. Three months aluminium is currently at $1,367, down $10.50.
Tin slumped to 16-month lows when the psychological $6,000 level was broken, with sell-stops sending the market down to $5,920, a $100 loss from Monday.
Lead hit $750, a new seven-month low, but attracted some commission house buying and moved back to an unchanged $756. A stock fall of 1,050 tonnes helped arrest the fall, traders said.
Zinc proved resilient around the $1,020 level, and was $3 higher at $1,019. Technically, prices are ranging between $1,015 and $1,030.
Nickel and alloy were softer at $7,080/90 and $1,220/30.
